clue.text: A group not bothered about chaps leaving

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the chaps
bothered means flustered or upset, so the word not is jumbled

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: A group of people who couldn't care less about a few men walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' looks like part of the story of chaps departing, but it is the noun definition; 'bothered' gives ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving someone or something behind is desertion, a synonym in noun form.

clue.text: Out-of-place athlete?

parts.note: an athlete who is 'out of place' finished outside the first three places in a race

explanation.surface: A sportsman who looks as if they don't belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-place' seems to mean misplaced, but here it means not among the placed finishers.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who fails to finish in the top places of a race is an unplaced runner.

clue.text: Warning having lost right old battle

indicators.note: having lost says a letter is taken out of the warning word

parts.note: an alarm is a warning

explanation.surface: An alert that has lost its correctness, perhaps about an old battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes the R out of ALARM, leaving ALAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was an 1836 siege in Texas, a famous battle of the Texas Revolution.

clue.text: Rebel Democrat insisted on change?

indicators.note: change? asks for the letters of insisted to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellious Democrat pushes hard for political change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' with its question mark is the anagram signal, not a political goal; it yields ISSIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident is a person who opposes official policy, so a rebel is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Without agreement, retreat

parts.note: without means lacking, as in no sugar
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Failing to reach agreement, one side withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' is a noun here, a secluded corner, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy corner or secluded hideaway, a snug place to withdraw to.

clue.text: Lift to reveal changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of to reveal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raising something up so a transformation can be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word for the passenger car the Americans name an elevator; both are synonyms.

clue.text: Board rebel battleship, partly capsized

indicators.note: capsized says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rebels board a warship, which then partly overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' finds ELBAT in 'rebel battleship' and 'capsized' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Board is an old word for a dining surface, as in 'bed and board', synonym for a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Kick member appearing as pirate

parts.note: to boot is to kick
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A kicking limb belongs to someone playing the part of a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate recordings or goods is to copy them illegally, the same as to make illicit copies.

clue.text: Simple article about the Italian church

indicators.note: about says these words go round the next piece

parts.note: basic means simple
il is Italian for the
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A plain write-up about an Italian church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the simple word and the article together round the Italian definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, especially one given special status by the Pope.

clue.text: Soft rock gets Blair in a lather?

definitions.meaning: a soft talc-based stone used for carving
read as '...', washing Tony Blair, his name shortened

explanation.surface: Mellow music makes a prime minister froth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was a British Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: This talc-rich mineral is notably soft, easily scratched and carved, so a soft rock.

clue.text: Supporter: 'Five-nil? Well done!'

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
V is the Roman numeral for five
nil is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A football fan cheers a five-nil victory.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is a cry of approval, applauding a fine performance.

clue.text: Piece on board that is green

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A chess piece that happens to be coloured green.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced, and a newcomer or novice is the noun sense here, used as a description.

clue.text: Important friend facing hearing when leader quits

indicators.note: facing says the friend comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: when leader quits says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A key friend facing a court hearing loses the chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leader quits' drops the T of TRIAL, leaving RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Material evidence is relevant and significant, so it is synonymous with important.

clue.text: Shark served with last of salad was tender

parts.note: a nurse shark is a kind of shark

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of salad

explanation.surface: A shark was served up with a side of salad, and it was tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' is a verb here: to tend, as a carer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone is to care for them as a carer would, past tense to match.

clue.text: Call on faithful to stand up

indicators.note: on says the call is placed above the faithful in this down clue

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
true means faithful or loyal

explanation.surface: A summons for loyal followers to rise to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that stands up holds good under scrutiny, sounding genuine and convincing.

clue.text: Being tactile could be moving

definitions.meaning: making physical contact with the hands

explanation.surface: Physical contact can stir the emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: physical contact, and emotionally stirring like a poignant scene.

clue.text: Singer first to be seen in piece of work by Queen

indicators.note: by says the queen sits beside the rest
to be seen in says the next piece sits inside the work

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work
first is written 1st, read as IST
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A singer makes a first appearance in a work by the rock band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1st, which crosswords read as IST; 'to be seen in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir member sings in a church or cathedral choir, so is a singer.

clue.text: Promise made by witches over a set of religious books

indicators.note: over places the witches above the rest in this down clue

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Witches make a pledge over a holy book.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn agreement or pledge, often binding, as in the biblical covenant.

clue.text: Authorise punitive measure

definitions.meaning: a penalty imposed, such as trade restrictions on a country

explanation.surface: Approving a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is a contronym: both official approval and a penalty for breaking rules.

clue.text: Some sense ancestors — at these?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people sense their ancestors at spiritualist sittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings where mediums claim to contact the dead are where some would sense forebears.

clue.text: Slough needs men in service

indicators.note: in says the men sit inside the service

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: The Berkshire town needs men to attend church.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it means a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or bog, and figuratively a mire one cannot escape.

clue.text: Spot what hen does in case of small eggs, initially

indicators.note: in puts the hen's action inside that case
case of takes the outside letters of small

parts.note: a hen pecks at grain

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of eggs

explanation.surface: A hen pecks around a box of small eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' means the outer letters only of 'small'; 'in' then puts the hen's action between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny mark or dot is a fleck, so spot is a synonym.

clue.text: One picking holes in fancy cake and tart

indicators.note: fancy says the letters of cake and tart are made into something elaborate, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone critical finds fault with a fancy cake and tart.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic picking holes in an argument assails it, an aggressor's role.

clue.text: Endless piracy ruined island

indicators.note: ruined says the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
Endless says the final letter of piracy is dropped

explanation.surface: Unchecked piracy has ruined an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops Y from PIRACY; 'ruined' rearranges PIRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian isle in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: End exercise to seize power in French town

parts.note: to die is to end

indicators.note: to seize says exercise grips the next piece

parts.note: PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Ending the workout to grab power in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a Channel port in Normandy, scene of the 1942 raid.

clue.text: Kind of line that's fruity, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: A type of line that sounds like fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted cord hung to find the vertical is called by this name, a builder's tool.

clue.text: Do business in Kent town

definitions.meaning: a seaside town on the Kent coast, Kent being a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: Trading in a coastal town.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to do business; this is also a seaside town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Dope from China going to Portugal

indicators.note: going to says the pal comes before the next piece

parts.note: china, from rhyming slang china plate = mate, means a pal
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Drugs shipped from China to Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' means mate, so china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a fool, as is a silly person called this name.

clue.text: Adult you and I hit is stunned

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
you and I together are we
struck means hit

explanation.surface: A grown-up we both hit is left stunned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overwhelmed with wonder leaves one amazed, as if stunned.

clue.text: Not reliable, sadly, and beyond the pale

indicators.note: sadly says the words not reliable are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Being unreliable is, sadly, unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the pale means outside acceptable behaviour, unbearable.
